title: Earthquake Response Simulation
cardImageAlt: Placeholder preview for Earthquake Response Simulation
headerImageAlt: Placeholder preview for Earthquake Response Simulation
summary: An animated simulation of the effectiveness of a student-designed earthquake response system
description: Shake It Off is a STEM case that teaches tectonics by having students design an earthquake warning system. I built the culminating piece of interactivity: an animated simulation where students choose sensor types and locations, then test their network against earthquakes from different epicenters. Sensors trigger as the waves reach them, and students see how quickly their system responded and how many people it warned in time.

I inherited the project when a coworker left and became its sole developer, working with a content designer, an art director, and a project manager. I finished the simulation in Vue 2 and TypeScript with d3.js and Grapes.js, tying it to the case's existing data so every student's design produced results that supported the lesson's learning goals.
The project was 6 months behind schedule when I took it over. I shipped it in 8 weeks.

title: Orbit Simulator
summary: An interactive simulation of orbital mechanics and satellite trajectories
description: Save a Satellite is a STEM case that ExploreLearning built in collaboration with NASA, where students act as spacecraft navigation engineers. They launch a communication satellite into a stable orbit, then steer it out of the path of space debris using what they've learned about gravity and Newton's laws. I built the orbit simulation at the heart of the case.

Students adjust the satellite's velocity and the pull of gravity, and the simulation shows the result in real time: the satellite crashes back to Earth, settles into a stable orbit or flies off into space, depending on the size and direction of their changes. The main challenge was to depict the physics in a way that was simple enough for the grade level and visually congruent with the animations built by the art team, while also being true to the core scientific principles we were teaching.
As the sole developer, I built it in Vue 2 and TypeScript with p5.js and Grapes.js, working with a content designer, an art director, an animator, and a project manager.

title: Protecting Permafrost
summary: An interactive project focused on strategies to protect permafrost regions
description: In Protecting Permafrost: Heat Transfer Highway, students play civil engineers protecting a highway in an Arctic Alaskan town, where thawing permafrost threatens the ground it's built on. They design heat transfer solutions to keep the ground frozen in a warming climate. I built the interactive design activity where students test their ideas.

Students drag materials onto SVG diagrams of the sections of road, and the activity grades their design against a rubric, giving feedback on how well the students allocated their material budget. The biggest challenge was in managing the precision of interactivity necessary within a component that needed to work within our preexisting Grapes.js interface. The component needed to be placeable on multiple pages and to work with varying amounts of materials while delivering consistent results.
As the sole developer, I built it in Vue 2 and TypeScript with Grapes.js, working with a content and design team.

title: Sound Wave Visualizer
cardImageAlt: Placeholder preview for Sound Wave Visualizer
headerImageAlt: Placeholder preview for Sound Wave Visualizer
summary: An interactive visualization of sound wave amplitude and frequency
description: Sound Off, Please! is a STEM case about noise pollution. Students act as acoustic engineers, working with an urban planner to understand how noise affects a community and to test ways to reduce it. I built the sound wave visualizer that helps students understand the relationship between frequency and amplitude in a sound wave.

Students change a sound wave's frequency and amplitude and see the wave redraw instantly, so they can connect what they see to the pitch and loudness of a tone that they could play by clicking a button.
As the sole developer, I built it in Vue 2 and TypeScript with d3.js and Grapes.js, working with a consulting developer and a design team.

title: NRG Advocacy
summary: An advocacy project focused on energy policy and community engagement
description: NRG needed a website to promote its grassroots advocacy work on energy policy topics. I built the site's front end from the designer's mockups in a Sketch file, making it fully responsive, with a PHP back end.
I was the sole front-end developer, working with LGND's designer and project manager.

title: Ending Pandemics Map
cardImageAlt: Placeholder preview for Ending Pandemics Map
headerImageAlt: Placeholder preview for Ending Pandemics Map
summary: An interactive map visualizing efforts to end pandemics
description: Ending Pandemics, a nonprofit working on disease surveillance and outbreak prevention, wanted to spread awareness of pandemics throughout history and what measures were taken to mitigate the spread of disease. With the agency LGND, I built an interactive map of that data.

The map is built with d3.js and jQuery. Visitors can pan and zoom on a global map to see locations of previous response programs to outbreaks, filter data to view specific program types, and click a program to see more details. Special care was taken to make sure the interactivity translated to mobile devices.
I was the sole front-end developer, working with LGND's designer and project manager.

title: Toyota Quizzes
summary: Two animated quizzes about political literacy for Toyota
description: With the agency LGND, I built a series of two animated quizzes for Toyota about political literacy, launched leading up to the 2022 midterm elections to encourage civic engagement.

Each quiz uses GreenSock animations to load questions and spin answers around in the fashion of a find-the-match style game, built with EJS templates, Sass, jQuery, and a PHP back end. One quiz questioned visitors on members of Biden's administration, and another focused on notable Hispanic politicians for Hispanic Heritage Month. The process involved developing a central template that was then extended out for each separate quiz.
I was the sole front-end developer, working with LGND's designer and project manager.

title: SparkFun À La Carte
summary: An application built for SparkFun's À La Carte circuit board design system
description: À La Carte was a SaaS product from SparkFun Electronics that let customers first design custom circuit boards by dragging and dropping components from menus, then order their finished board. I worked on it as a full-stack developer at SparkFun.
I built front-end components in Angular and the APIs behind them in Node.js and MongoDB, for functions such as updating the board and checking against design constraints.
I worked within a team of 8 software engineers.

description: Greater Washington Partnership, a group of business leaders in the Baltimore–Washington–Richmond region, published a 7-solution plan to improve how people get around the greater Washington, D.C. area. With the agency LGND, I built an 8-page website that explains the plan.

title: Social Explorer
summary: Thesis project for my Master's degree in Emergent Digital Practices
description: For my Master's thesis in Emergent Digital Practices, I built an interactive Node.js app that I titled Social Explorer. Users control an abstracted avatar and proceed through a series of simulated social environments meant to visualize feelings of social anxiety and create a visual language for unspoken interactions.
I built this project with Express, Node.js, and p5.js. My thesis advisors were Laleh Mehran and Chris Coleman.

Abstract: For my project, I sought to develop a web application that consciously harnesses its rhetorical power in order to develop a visual and procedural form of diffractive representation, an alternative to a commonly held and unquestioned reflexive representation of the world. A reflexive representation measures sameness; a diffractive representation measures patterns of difference. My project, Social Explorer, is an online experience in which the user progresses through a series of simulated social environments in an attempt to create relationships with others. I demonstrate diffractive entanglements through the depiction of social anxieties felt in everyday interactions. The goal of this project is to visually and algorithmically represent sensations of social friction in a playable experience in order to gain a visual understanding of diffractive relationships.
